subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Mensuration 3D — Volume and Surface Area (W11 B2)

questions.stem: The volume of a cube is 343 cm³. What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Volume of cube = a³ = 343 → a = ∛343 = 7 cm. Total surface area = 6a² = 6×7² = 6×49 = 294 cm². Trap: 216 = 6×6²=6×36 (wrong edge=6); 196 = 4×7²=4×49 (lateral surface only, not total); 324 = 6×7.35² (computation error).

questions.stem: A cuboid has dimensions 8 cm × 6 cm × 5 cm. What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Total surface area of cuboid = 2(lb + bh + lh) where l=8, b=6, h=5. = 2(8×6 + 6×5 + 8×5) = 2(48 + 30 + 40) = 2×118 = 236 cm². Verify: lb=48, bh=30, lh=40; sum=118; ×2=236 ✓. Trap: 240 = 2(8×6 + 6×6 + 8×6) uses wrong value; 280 = 2(8+6+5)×... (lateral surface method misapplied).

questions.stem: The radius of a cylinder is 7 cm and height is 10 cm. What is the volume? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: B is correct. Volume of cylinder = πr²h = (22/7)×7²×10 = (22/7)×49×10 = 22×7×10 = 1540 cm³. Short trick: (22/7)×49 = 22×7 = 154; then ×10 = 1540. Trap: 1470 = πr²h with r=7,h=10 but uses π=3 (wrong); 1760 = 2πrh×r (confused with lateral surface); 1340 = computational error.

questions.stem: The curved surface area of a cylinder is 440 cm² and height is 10 cm. What is the radius? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: B is correct. CSA of cylinder = 2πrh = 440. 2×(22/7)×r×10 = 440. (44/7)×10×r = 440. 440r/7 = 440. r = 7 cm. Verify: 2×(22/7)×7×10 = 2×22×10 = 440 ✓. Trap: 14 = doubles the radius (confuses radius with diameter); 5 = half of 10 (random division).

The slant height of a cone is 13 cm and radius is 5 cm. What is the curved surface area? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: A is correct. CSA of cone = πrl = (22/7)×5×13 = (22×65)/7 = 1430/7 = 204 2/7 cm². Verify: 22×5=110; 110×13=1430; 1430÷7=204.28=204 2/7 ✓. Note: no need to find height (which = √(13²−5²)=√(169−25)=√144=12 cm) since slant height l is given directly. Trap: 220 = (22/7)×5×14 (uses l=14 instead of 13).

questions.stem: A cone has base radius 7 cm and height 24 cm. What is its slant height?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Slant height l = √(r²+h²) = √(7²+24²) = √(49+576) = √625 = 25 cm. Recognise this as a Pythagorean triple: 7-24-25 ✓. Trap: 26 = √(7²+25²)=√674≈26 (wrong — 25 is the slant height, not height); 31 = √(7²+30²) (wrong values).

questions.stem: If the radius of a sphere is doubled, by what factor does its volume increase?
questions.explanation: D is correct. Volume of sphere ∝ r³. If r → 2r, new volume = (4/3)π(2r)³ = (4/3)π×8r³ = 8×original volume. Volume increases 8 times. Short trick: volume scales as (ratio of radii)³ = 2³ = 8. Trap: 2 = linear scaling (forgets it's cubic); 4 = surface area scaling (area scales as r², not volume); 6 = common wrong answer for cubic scaling.

questions.stem: A hollow cylinder (pipe) has outer radius 7 cm, inner radius 5 cm, and length 14 cm. What is the volume of metal used? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: B is correct. Volume of metal in hollow cylinder = pi(R^2 - r^2)h where R=7, r=5, h=14. = (22/7) x (49 - 25) x 14 = (22/7) x 24 x 14 = 22 x 24 x 2 = 1056 cm^3. Step check: 49 - 25 = 24; 24 x 14 = 336; 336 x 22 = 7392; 7392 / 7 = 1056. Short cut: (22/7) x 24 x 14 = 22 x 24 x 2 = 22 x 48 = 1056. Trap: 1100 = uses wrong ring dimensions; 1048 = off-by-8 computation error.

questions.stem: A metallic sphere of radius 3 cm is melted and recast into a cylinder of radius 3 cm. What is the height of the cylinder? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: B is correct. Volume of sphere = volume of cylinder (same metal, no wastage). (4/3)πr₁³ = πr₂²h. Here r₁=3 (sphere), r₂=3 (cylinder). (4/3)π×27 = π×9×h. 36π = 9πh. h = 36/9 = 4 cm. Verify: sphere volume = (4/3)π×27=36π; cylinder volume = π×9×4=36π ✓. Short trick: when radii are equal, h = (4/3)r = (4/3)×3 = 4.
